summary:
Unmatched brackets split the string into independent pieces, and the longest balanced stretch lives between two
of them. A stack of indices finds every match and measures each balanced run from the last unmatched position:
O(n). Two counter passes (left-to-right and right-to-left) do the same in O(1) space.

question.md:
Return the length of the longest **contiguous** piece of `s` that is balanced.

- **Contiguous:** `()(()` has `()` and the inner `()`; the longest is 2, not 4.
- **Balanced pieces can sit side by side:** `()()` is one balanced stretch of length 4.
- **Size:** up to 10⁵ characters, so trying all O(n²) pieces is too slow.

think.md:
Take `)(()())(()`. The `)` at position 0 can never be matched, and neither can the `(` at position 7. Everything else is
matched, so the balanced stretches are positions 1…6 (`(()())`, length 6) and 8…9 (`()`, length 2). The answer is
6.

think.caption: Unmatched brackets (marked) act as walls; the longest balanced run between walls wins.

think.md:
So the job is: find which brackets are unmatched, and measure the gaps between them. A stack of indices does
this naturally if it keeps, at its bottom, the position of the last "wall" (unmatched `)`, or −1 at the start):
after any `)` is matched, the current balanced run reaches back to just after the index on top of the stack.

approaches.title: Scan from every start

idea.md: For each start i, walk right keeping the depth (+1 for `(`, −1 for `)`). If it goes negative, nothing starting at i can extend further: stop. Whenever it's 0, `i … j` is balanced.

build: For each j ≥ i: update depth; stop if negative; record `j − i + 1` when depth is 0.

lines.text: Extend one character at a time.
A `)` with nothing open: no balanced piece from i can contain it.

steps.text: Start 1, end 6: depth back to 0. New best 6.

walk.title: From every start, scan right keeping depth; stop when it goes negative; record lengths where depth returns to 0.

limits.md: Each start re-reads the same characters. Matching brackets once with a stack gives every balanced run directly.

approaches.title: Stack of indices with a boundary

idea.md: Start the stack with −1 (a virtual wall). `(` → push its index. `)` → pop; if the stack is now empty, this `)` is unmatched: push its index as the new wall; otherwise the balanced run ending here starts right after the index on top, so its length is `i − top`.

build: `)` → pop; empty → push i; else best = max(best, i − top).

lines.text: The bottom of the stack is always the last wall; −1 stands for "before the string".
Try to match: pop the most recent `(` (or the wall, if none is open).
Nothing was open: this `)` is unmatched and becomes the new wall.
Matched: everything after the index now on top is balanced up to i.

steps.text: ')' at 0 has no partner: it becomes the new boundary.
')' at 3 matches; balanced run from 2 to 3: length 2.
')' at 5 matches; balanced run from 2 to 5: length 4.
')' at 6 matches; balanced run from 1 to 6: length 6.
')' at 9 matches; balanced run from 8 to 9: length 2.

walk.title: Stack of indices, starting with −1 as a 'last invalid position'. Push '(' indices; on ')', pop, then measure from the new top.

limits.md: The stack can hold up to n indices. With one bracket kind, counts of `(` and `)` can find the same runs in O(1) space, at the cost of a second pass.

approaches.title: Two counter passes

idea.md:
Left to right, count `open` and `close`. When equal, the piece since the last reset is balanced: record
`2 × close`. When `close > open`, reset both (that `)` is a wall).

That pass misses pieces where `(` stays ahead until the end, like `(()`. So do a mirror pass right to left:
record when equal, reset when `open > close`. The best of both passes is the answer.

build: Left-to-right pass with the reset rule `close > open`.
Right-to-left pass with the reset rule `open > close`.

lines.text: Left to right: equal counts mean the piece since the last reset is balanced. More `)` than `(` can never recover, so start over after it. This pass misses balanced pieces followed only by surplus `(`.
Right to left with the roles reversed: more `(` than `)` (seen from the right) is the dead end. This catches exactly what the first pass missed.
The best length from either pass.

steps.text: → 0: more ')' than '(': nothing balanced can cross here; reset.
The right-to-left pass catches runs like '(()' that the first pass misses. Best overall 6.

walk.title: Two counters, two passes. Left to right: reset when ')' outnumbers '('; record when equal. Then right to left with the roles swapped.

takeaways.md:
- Keep a **sentinel index** (−1 or the last unmatched `)`) at the bottom of an index stack to measure balanced runs.
- With a single bracket kind, two counter passes in opposite directions replace the stack.
- Unmatched brackets are walls: no balanced stretch can cross one.
